newsitem.title: UK: Safeway extends gains after results. [CORRECTED 11:20 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Safeway extends gains after results. [CORRECTED 11:20 GMT]

text.p: Shares in Safeway Plc rose on Thursday, extending Wednesday's gains after positive press comment on the supermarket group's results showing like-for-like sales rising a better-than-expected 3.7 percent (corrects from three percent).

The Financial Times' Lex column said the trading environment for the supermarket groups had stabilised, adding that Safeway's twenty percent discount to the prospective price-earnings ratio on the market as a whole therefore "looks excessive."

Against the trend of the UK stock market overall, where the FTSE 100 was down 20.9 points at 4,666.0, Safeway shares were up 5p at 359-1/2 by 0826 GMT in volume of 1.4 million shares, after on Wednesday rising 23-1/2p.
Market sources said BZW raised Safeway to a "buy" and said it would switch aggressively out of J. Sainsbury Plc, down 7p at 373-1/2.
Analysts at the brokerage were not immediately available for comment.
Meanwhile, Goldman Sachs repeated an "outperform" rating on Safeway, though Goldman analysts were also not immediately available for comment.
